newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian group says PA undermines rule of law.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian group says PA undermines rule of law.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority is eroding the rule of law in areas it controls through arbitrary arrests, disregard of court rulings and interference of security forces in the judiciary, a rights group said on Tuesday.

"The Palestinian Authority has until now not respected the judicial system and didn't even try to protect it or defend it," Palestinian Human Rights Monitoring Group (PHRMG) Executive Director Bassem Eid told reporters.

The group released a report on what it said was widespread Palestinian Authority abuse and neglect of the West Bank and Gaza judicial system -- built on Ottoman, British, Jordanian, Egyptian and Israeli laws -- since the PA was formed in 1994.

"The most terrible thing is the intervention of security services in the judicial system," Eid said, alleging that security officials and their friends and relatives often refused to appear in court or subverted witnesses.
The report detailed the cases of 117 jailed Palestinians who have been held without charge for more than one year. It said many others had been held for shorter periods.
In a number of cases, detainees were reported to have been beaten into signing confessions that they were collaborators for Israel or accusing others of working for the Jewish state.
Many detainees listed were arrested for blatantly political reasons, the report charged.

Eid said the summary trial of three Palestinians who were arrested, tried and sentenced to long prison terms on Saturday for killing an Israeli taxi driver just hours after the man's body was found showed the PA's disregard for due process.
"It wasn't a trial. These people were just sentenced for life imprisonment within half an hour," Eid said.
Eid said Palestinian Attorney General Fayez Abu Rahma had criticised the hasty trial but his declaration carried no weight because Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had ordered the case go forward.

He said Arafat appointed Abu Rahma, who took office last month, to show he was trying to improve the overall situation. Abu Rahma's predecessor, Khaled al-Kidra, was widely criticised by rights groups.
In a written response to the PHRMG report, Abu Rahma declared the general need to modify detention laws in the West Bank and Gaza but did not address many of the report's findings.
Abu Rahma was not available for immediate comment. He had told reporters this week he had freed about 40 detainees since taking office.
"The Palestinian Authority suffers from many difficulties resulting from its interim nature -- a stepping stone between occupation and an independent Palestinian state," the PHRMG report said.

"We cannot include the suppression of free speech and political activity through detentions, the detention of suspects for over two years without a trial and the unwillingness to respect the decisions of the judiciary as part of those 'difficulties.'"
